plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen subshrub with narrow gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers held on slender stems. It is widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields for its essential oil and attracts large numbers of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', since the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large daisy-like flower head made of many tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral, surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, a behavior called heliotropism.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early July through September in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Native to North America; grown extensively in Ukraine, Russia, the Great Plains of the USA, and France
plants.funFact: Once mature, sunflower heads stop tracking the sun and permanently face east, which warms them in the morning and attracts more pollinators.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves that rise above the water and showy, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. Its leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking from June to August
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; found in ponds and wetlands in India, China, Vietnam, and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their temperature to about 30-35°C (86-95°F), even when the surrounding air is cooler, thanks to a heat-producing process similar to that of warm-blooded animals.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head of any protea, a bowl-shaped bloom of stiff pointed bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, well-drained soils of fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere winter and spring, with blooms beginning around June and July
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its ancient lineage predates the breakup of the supercontinent Gondwana.
